en: To provoke someone to do wrong, especially by promising a reward; to entice.
To attract; to allure.

tempt.ety: From Middle English tempten, from Old French tempter (French: tenter), from Latin temptare, from tentare (“to handle, touch, try, test, tempt”), frequentative of tendere (“to stretch”). Displaced native English costning (“temptation”).

ex.en: I am tempted to doubt your friendship.
ex.ja: 私は君の友情を疑いたくなる。

ex.en: She was tempted to come with me.
ex.ja: 彼女は私のお供をするように仕向けられた。

ex.en: What tempted him to come home?
ex.ja: 何が彼を帰宅する気にさせたのか。

note.ja: ラテン語 temptare（試す・さぐる）から。「試してそそのかす」→「誘惑する」。attempt（試みる）も同じ。

en: An attack made by moving the sword parallel to its length and landing with the point.
A push, stab, or lunge forward.
To make advance with force.
To force something upon someone.

thrust.ety: From Middle English þrusten, from Old Norse þrysta, from Proto-Germanic *þrustijaną, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *trewd-.

ex.en: Don't thrust your knife into the cheese.
ex.ja: チーズの中へナイフを突き刺したりするな。

ex.en: I thrust my hand into my pocket.
ex.ja: 私はポケットに手を突っ込んだ。

ex.en: I thrust my way through the crowd.
ex.ja: 私は人込みを押し分けて進んだ。

note.ja: 北欧語 þrýsta（押す）から。threat（脅し）と同系とされる。「強く押す」→「推進力・要点」。

en: A set of three connected works—usually dramas, literary pieces, films, or musical compositions—all related by theme, characters, or setting.

note.ja: tri（3つ）+ log（言葉・物語）+ y。3つの物語 →「三部作」。

en: The act of accusing.
A formal charge brought against a person in a court of law.

accusation.ety: First attested in the late 14th century. Doublet of accusatio. More at accuse. Equivalent to accuse + -ation.

ex.en: She's not here to defend herself against these accusations.
ex.ja: 彼女はこれらの告発に対して自らを弁護するためにここへ来たわけではない。

ex.en: He is under a false accusation.
ex.ja: 彼は無実の罪で告発されている。

ex.en: She didn't come here to defend herself against these accusations.
ex.ja: 彼女はこれらの告発に対して自らを弁護するためにここへ来たわけではない。

note.ja: accuse（責める）+ -ation。ad（〜に）+ causa（訴訟・理由）。「訴えを起こすこと」→「非難・告発」。cause と同じ。

Acknowledgment.
To put upon a fixed allowance (especially of provisions and drink).
To supply in a fixed and limited quantity.

Determined by impulse rather than reason; often connoting heavy-handedness.
Anything arbitrary, such as an arithmetical value or a fee.

ex.ja: 私たちがポルトガルへ行こうと決めたのはまったくの気まぐれだった。

ex.ja: これは自律的な機械です。

Food containing poison or a harmful additive to kill animals that are pests.
To attract with bait; to entice.
To affix bait to a trap or a fishing hook or fishing line.
Obvious; blatant.
Well-known; famous; renowned.

Cognate with German Beize (“mordant, corrosive fluid; marinade”), Old English bāt (“that which can be bitten, food, bait”).

ex.ja: 彼は釣り針に生き餌をつけた。

ex.ja: 私は釣り針にえさを付けた。

en: To make a short, loud, explosive noise with the vocal organs (said of animals, especially dogs).
To make a clamor; to make importunate outcries.
The short, loud, explosive sound uttered by a dog, a fox, and some other animals.
An abrupt loud vocal utterance.
The sound of a dog barking.

bark.ety:
From Middle English barken, berken, borken, from Old English beorcan (“to bark”), from the Proto-West Germanic *berkan (“to bark”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerg- (“to make a noise, growl, bark”), from *bʰer- (“to drone, hum, buzz”).
Cognate with Icelandic berkja (“to bark, bluster”), Icelandic barki (“throat, windpipe”), dialectal Lithuanian burgė́ti (“to growl, grumble, grouch, quarrel”), Serbo-Croatian brbljati (“to murmur”). For the noun, compare Old English beorc, bearce (“barking”).

ex.en: I heard a dog barking in the distance.
ex.ja: 犬が遠くで吠えているのが聞こえた。

ex.en: The dog kept barking all through the night.
ex.ja: 犬は一晩中吠えどおしだった。

ex.en: I hear a dog barking in the woods.
ex.ja: 森の中で犬がほえているのが聞こえる。

note.ja: 「ほえる」は古英語 beorcan（擬音的）から。「樹皮」は北欧語 börkr からで別語。

en: An item of clothing, usually underwear worn to support the breasts.

bra.ety: Clipping of brassiere, borrowed from French brassière, from Old French braciere (originally a lining inside armor to protect the arm, but later a garment), from Old French brace (“arm”), from Latin bracchia, plural of Latin bracchium (“forearm”), from Ancient Greek βραχίων (brakhíōn, “forearm”), from Proto-Hellenic *brəkʰús (“short”) (because the forearm is shorter than the upper arm), inherited from Proto-Indo-European *mréǵʰus.

ex.en: Yumiko has a push-up bra.
ex.ja: 優美子には谷間を強調するブラジャーがある。

ex.en: Please take off all your clothes except your underpants and bra.
ex.ja: パンツとブラジャー以外は全部脱いでください。

ex.en: Now that you mention it, she also needs a bra and panties.
ex.ja: 店員さんがそう言うなら、ブラジャーとパンティーも買ってってやろう。

note.ja: フランス語 brassière（胴着）の短縮。bras（腕）から。

en: The state of being brothers or a brother (also figuratively).
An association of people for any purpose, such as a society of monks; a fraternity.

brotherhood.ety: From Middle English brotherhod, equivalent to brother + -hood, from earlier brotherhede, alteration (influenced by suffixes in -hood, -head) of brotherrede (“brotherhood, fraternity”), from Old English brōþorrǣden (“brotherhood, fellowship”), equivalent to brother + -red (see brotherred). More at brother, -red. Piecewise doublet of friarhood.

ex.en: "Freedom, Equality, Brotherhood" is also Haiti's motto.
ex.ja: 「自由・平等・博愛」はハイチ共和国のスローガンでもある。

note.ja: brother（兄弟）+ -hood（状態・集団）。「兄弟の間柄」→「兄弟愛・団体」。

A practitioner of the religion and philosophy of Buddhism.
A follower of the Indian religious and spiritual teacher, Buddha.

en: The act of conveying; carrying.
A means of conveyance.

ex.ja: ファッションモデルは身のこなしがよくなければならない。

ex.en: The couple took a horse carriage that evening.
ex.ja: 夫婦は、その日の夕方、馬車に乗りました。

ex.en: These are not first-class carriages.
ex.ja: ここは一等車ではありません。

note.ja: carry（運ぶ）+ -age。ラテン語 carrus（荷車）から。「運ぶもの」→「馬車・客車・運送」。car、career と同じ。

en: To make or become clear or bright by freeing from impurities or turbidity.
To make or become clear or easily understood; to explain or resolve in order to remove doubt or obscurity.

clarify.ety: From Middle English clarifien, from Old French clarifiier, from Latin clārificō, clārificāre; clārus (“clear”) + faciō, facere (“make”). Semantically clear + -ify.

ex.en: I appreciate your help in clarifying this.
ex.ja: この件を明らかにするのを手伝っていただいて感謝してます。

ex.ja: 彼に質問した後で彼のいいたかったことが明確になった。

note.ja: ラテン語 clarificare ＝ clarus（明るい）+ facere。「明らかにする」。clear と同じ。

en: The act or process of compiling or gathering together from various sources.
That which is compiled; especially, a book or document composed of materials gathering from other books or documents.

compilation.ety: English compile + -ation, from Middle French, from Latin compilatio (“a raking together, a plundering, a collection of documents”).

ex.en: Attached is the draft compilation.
ex.ja: 草案を添付します。

ex.en: He devoted his whole life to compilation of the dictionary.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯を辞書の編さんに費やした。

note.ja: compile（編集する）+ -ation。ラテン語 compilare（かき集める）。「集めてまとめたもの」→「編集・コンピレーション」。

en: To set up; to establish; to enact.
To make up; to compose; to form.

constitute.ety: From Middle English constituten, from Latin cōnstitūtum, neuter of cōnstitūtus, past participle of Latin cōnstituō (“to put in place; set up; establish”), from con- (“with”) + statuō (“to put up; establish”).

ex.en: He was constituted representative of the party.
ex.ja: 彼は党の代表に立てられた。

ex.en: Six members constitute the committee.
ex.ja: ６人の委員でその委員会を構成する。

ex.en: The universe on the earth is constituted of atoms.
ex.ja: 飛球上の万物は原子からなっている。

en: Reciprocal exchange of civilities, especially conversation between persons by means of letters.
Newspaper or news stories.

correspondence.ety: From Middle English correspondence, from Latin correspondentia. By surface analysis, correspond + -ence.

ex.en: We have carried on a correspondence for years.
ex.ja: 私たちは何年も文通をつづけている。

ex.en: I have some correspondence to deal with.
ex.ja: 私は返事を書くべき手紙がいくらかある。

ex.en: She'll be seeing to your correspondence while Miss Cobb's away.
ex.ja: コブさんがいない間あなたの通信事務の仕事をしてくれることになります。

en: Worthy to be desired; pleasing; agreeable.
Sexually attractive.
A thing that people want; something that is desirable.

desirable.ety:
From Old French desirable.
Morphologically desire + -able.

ex.en: A devastating earthquake hit the state capital.

ex.en: They confirmed the importance of strengthening global precautions in order to prevent devastating losses.
ex.ja: 壊滅的な被害を防ぐために世界的な警戒を強化していく重要性を確認した。

To put up by the fitting together of materials or parts.
To cause to stand up or out.

ex.ja: この像は十年前に作られた。

A defect, fault, or imperfection, especially one that is hidden.
To add a flaw to, to make imperfect or defective.
To become imperfect or defective; to crack or break.

ex.ja: 発言するたびにボロが出る。

genesis.ety: Borrowed from Latin genesis (“generation, nativity”), from Ancient Greek γένεσις (génesis, “origin, source, beginning”). Related to Ancient Greek γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to be produced, become, be”). Doublet of kind, gens, and jati.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 genesis（誕生・起源）から。gignesthai（生まれる）。gene、generate と同じ gen。聖書の「創世記」。

en: Of or relating to geography.
A move to another place in the hope of curing an addiction etc.

geographical.ety: From Late Latin geōgraphicus + -al. By surface analysis, geography + -ical.

ex.ja: この店は地の利をえている。

ex.en: The geographical features here are similar to those of our prefecture.
ex.ja: ここの地理的特徴は私達の県のそれと似ている。

note.ja: geography + -ical。ギリシャ語 gē（大地）+ graphein（書く）。「大地を記述する」。

en: Not complete; not finished.
Of a flower, wanting any of the usual floral organs.
A designation of being incomplete.

incomplete.ety: From Middle English incomplete, incompleet, from Late Latin incomplētus, from in- (“un-; not”) + complētus (“complete”), equivalent to in- (“not”) + complete.

ex.ja: 中途半端な文ね。

ex.ja: このレポート、中途半端だな。

ex.en: This list is incomplete.
ex.ja: このリストは未完成です。

A creamy white color, the color of ivory.

ex.en: He carved designs in ivory.

ex.en: The peace we have today is the result of lengthy peace talks.
ex.ja: 長い和平交渉を経て、現在の平和がある。

ex.ja: 私を死ぬほど退屈させたのは、彼の長ったらしい話だった。

note.ja: length（長さ）+ -y。「長い・長ったらしい」。

en: To impose (a tax or fine) to collect monies due, or to confiscate property.
To raise or collect by assessment; to exact by authority.
The act of levying.
A conscription action.

lever (“to raise”), from Latin lēvāre (“to raise, lift”).

ex.ja: 日本では、ほとんどの物やサービスに５％の消費税がかけられる。

ex.en: A 5% consumption tax is levied on purchases of most goods and services.
ex.ja: ほとんどの物やサービスの購入に対しては５％の消費税がかかる。

ex.en: An income tax is levied on any income that exceeds deductions.
ex.ja: 所得税は控除額を上回るいかなる所得にもかかる。

en: The practice of manipulating or the state of being manipulated.

ex.ja: 彼はその教授の話し方を真似してからかった。

ex.en: People once mocked the idea that the earth is round.
ex.ja: 地球が円いという考えをかつて人々はちょう笑した。

ex.en: The boy is always mocked by his classmates.
ex.ja: 少年はいつもクラスメートにばかにされている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 mocquer（あざける）から。「あざける」→ まねてからかう →「模擬の・にせの」（mock exam 模擬試験）。

en: An article of jewelry that is worn around the neck, most often made of a string of precious metal, pearls, gems, beads or shells, and som…
Anything resembling a necklace in shape.
To informally execute by necklacing; by setting on fire a petrol-filled rubber tyre which has been put around the bound victim's neck.

en: A cavity, hollow, or recess, generally within the thickness of a wall, for a statue, bust, or other erect ornament.
Any similar position, literal or figurative.
To place in a niche.
To specialize in a niche, or particular narrow section of the market.
Pertaining to or intended for a market niche; having specific appeal; obscure.

niche.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French niche, from Middle French niche, from Old French niche, from nicher (“to make a nest”) (modern French nicher), from Vulgar Latin *nīdicāre, from Latin nīdus (“nest”). Doublet of nidus and nide via Latin and nest via Proto-Indo-European; also related to nyas.

ex.en: U.S. companies are working to find a niche in the Japanese economy.
ex.ja: アメリカの企業は、日本経済の中に活動の場を見いだそうとしています。

ex.en: He's adept at jumping into profitable niches.
ex.ja: 彼は小さい穴場を見つけて稼ぐのが得意です。

note.ja: フランス語 niche（壁のくぼみ）から。nicher（巣を作る）。「収まるくぼみ」→「適所・すき間市場」。

en: Dark, faint or indistinct.
Hidden, out of sight or inconspicuous.
To render obscure; to darken; to make dim; to keep in the dark; to hide; to make less visible, intelligible, legible, glorious, beautiful…
To hide, put out of sight etc.

obscure.ety: From Middle English obscure, from Old French obscur, from Latin obscūrus (“dark, dusky, indistinct”), from ob- + *scūrus, from Proto-Italic *skoiros, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱeh₃-. Doublet of oscuro.

ex.ja: 事故原因はまだはっきりしていない。

ex.en: There are some obscure points in his proposal.
ex.ja: 彼の提案はいくつか分かりにくい点がある。

ex.en: The meaning of this sentence is obscure.
ex.ja: この文の意味は不明瞭だ。

note.ja: ob（覆って）+ scurus（覆われた）。「覆い隠された」→「はっきりしない・無名の」。

en: A covered entrance to a building, whether taken from the interior, and forming a sort of vestibule within the main wall, or projecting wi…

porch.ety: From Middle English porche, from Old French, from Latin porticus (“portico”). Doublet of portego, portico, and porticus.

ex.en: Mary would often sit alone on the porch.
ex.ja: メアリーは、ベランダでひとり座っていることがよくあった。

ex.en: I think Tom is out on the porch.
ex.ja: トムはポーチに出てると思う。

ex.en: The cat came in through the porch door.
ex.ja: ネコがベランダに入ってきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 porticus（柱廊）から。porta（門）。「入り口の屋根付きの所」→「玄関・ポーチ」。port（港・門）と同系。

en: To paint or draw the likeness of.
To represent by an image or look.

portray.ety: From Middle English portray, from Middle French portraire.

note.ja: por（= pro 前へ）+ tray（引く・描く）。前へ引き出して描く →「描く・演じる」。portrait（肖像画）。

en: The act of offering (an idea) for consideration.
An idea, plan, or suggestion offered.
To make an offer or suggestion to (someone).
To make a suggestion of sexual intercourse to (someone with whom one is not sexually involved).

proposition.ety: From Middle English proposicioun, from Old French proposicion, from Latin prōpositiō, from the verb prōponō.

ex.ja: 耳寄りな話がある。

A period of low temperatures that causes a reduction in species; ice age.

recession.ety: Borrowed from Latin recessiō, from recēdō (“recede, retreat”), from re- (“back”) + cēdō (“to go”). By surface analysis, recess + -ion.

ex.ja: 来年は不況が避けられませんよ。

ex.ja: 世界はいま不況におちいっている。

en: Of or relating to the spine.

A spinal anesthesia.

To cause something to spiral.

A generally low, narrow, pointed, usually sandy peninsula or bar.
To impale on a spit; to pierce with a sharp object.
To use a spit to cook; to attend to food that is cooking on a spit.

ex.ja: シンガポールでは道路に唾を吐くのは犯罪です。

en: The sound made by an object hitting a liquid.
A small amount of liquid.
To hit or agitate liquid so that part of it separates from the principal liquid mass.
(of a liquid) To disperse suddenly as a result of an impulse; to splatter.

splash.ety: Probably an alteration of plash (compare spatter, spill for the initial s-).

ex.ja: 魚が水中で水を跳ね上げているのが見えた。

ex.en: A passing car splashed my coat with water.
ex.ja: 通過した車が私のコートに水をはねかけた。

ex.en: A passing car splashed water on us.
ex.ja: 通りがかりの車が私たちに水をはねた。

note.ja: 擬音語。plash（水がはねる音）に強めの s が付いた形。

en: Coming one after the other in a series.
Of, or relating to a succession; hereditary.

ex.en: It is hard to win four successive games.
ex.ja: 試合に４連勝するのは難しい。

ex.en: I went there by myself, often on successive evenings.
ex.ja: そこへ一人で、しばしば何日も続けて夜、行った。

ex.en: He won four successive world championships.
ex.ja: 彼は世界選手権で４連覇を成し遂げた。

note.ja: succeed（続く）+ -ive。sub + cedere（行く）。「後に続く」→「連続する」。success と同じ。

en: Any fictional crime-fighting character, often with supernatural powers or equipment, in popular children's and fantasy literature; a fict…
A particularly renowned real-world hero, or one who has seemingly impossible abilities.

superhero.ety: From super- + hero. First attested in 1917.

ex.en: Who's your favourite superhero?
ex.ja: あなたのお気に入りのスーパーヒーローは誰ですか。

ex.en: Even superheroes need an occasional break.
ex.ja: スーパーヒーローにも、時には休息が必要だ。

ex.en: Tom's favorite superhero is Superman.
ex.ja: トムが一番好きなスーパーヒーローは、スーパーマンなんだ。

note.ja: super（超えた）+ hero（英雄）。「超人的な英雄」。

en: Done at the proper time or within the proper time limits; prompt.
Happening or appearing at the proper time.
In compliance with applicable time limits.

timely.ety: From Middle English timely, tymely, timliche, from Old English tīmlīc (adjective) and tīmlīċe (“in good time; timely; soon”, adverb), equivalent to time + -ly. Cognate with Danish timelig, Swedish timlig, Icelandic tímalegur, tímanlegur.

ex.en: He made his timely escape from the stock market crash.
ex.ja: 彼は株の大暴落をうまくかわしていました。

ex.ja: その声明はときを得ていなかった。

ex.en: You must perform all assignments in a timely manner.
ex.ja: 割り当てられた仕事はすみやかにやらなければならない。

note.ja: time（時）+ -ly。「時にかなった」→「タイミングのよい」。

en: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
The contents or capacity of such a vessel.
To plant, set, or store in a tub.
To bathe in a tub.

tub.ety: From Middle English tubbe, tobbe, from Middle Dutch tubbe or Middle Low German tubbe, tobbe, further etymology unknown. Considered to be unrelated to tube.

ex.en: The tub ran over while she was on the phone.
ex.ja: 彼女が電話をしている間にふろ桶があふれた。

ex.en: Tom filled the tub with water.
ex.ja: トムは浴槽に水をためた。

ex.en: How much longer will it take for the tub to fill?
ex.ja: 後どのくらいでお風呂のお湯いっぱいになる？

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 tubbe（おけ）から。「おけ」→「浴槽」。bathtub。

Of, relating to, or being an undergraduate.

en: To take upon oneself; to start, to embark on.
To commit oneself (to an obligation, activity etc.).
The passing of slower traffic on the curbside rather than on the side closest to oncoming traffic.

undertake.ety: From Middle English undertaken; equivalent to under- + take (after undernim).

ex.ja: その事業は最初から失敗だった。

ex.en: I have a mind to undertake the work.
ex.ja: その仕事を引き受けようと思っている。

ex.ja: 彼のおじが彼の責任を負うだろう。

note.ja: under + take。「（仕事を）下から引き受ける」→「引き受ける・着手する」。undertaker は「葬儀屋」（葬儀を引き受ける人）。

An atom of this element.

ex.en: When he left the place, it was in an utter mess.
ex.ja: 調査官がその場を去る時、そこはまったく目茶苦茶だった。

ex.ja: 彼女は一言も発せられなかった。

ex.ja: 彼女は今では私には全くの他人です。

note.ja: 「発する」は中世オランダ語 uteren（外に出す）、out から。「まったくの」は古英語 ūterra（より外の）からで、どちらも out の仲間。

The inflated ball used in such a game.

A shout.

dry (of cow)

ex.ja: 何人かの運転手は笑ったりわめいたりしていた。

ex.ja: 彼は兵士たちに大声を上げて命令した。

To enclose in typographical brackets.

To deal with.

ex.ja: その国は財政危機に直面している。

ex.ja: 我々は難局に直面している。

ex.en: I am confronted with a difficult problem.
ex.ja: 私は困難な問題に直面している。

To grow across a surface rather than upwards.
The movement of something that creeps (like worms or snails).
A relatively small gradual change, variation or deviation (from a planned value) in a measure.

ex.en: Fear crept into my heart and settled there.
ex.ja: 恐ろしさが私の心に忍び込み、そこに残った。

ex.en: Jim had hardly got home when he crept into bed.
ex.ja: ジムは家に着くとすぐにベッドにもぐり込んだ。

ex.en: The baby crept into the room.
ex.ja: 赤ちゃんは部屋に這ってきた。

note.ja: 古英語 crēopan（這う）から。「這う」→ そっと近づく →「忍び寄る」→ 気味の悪いやつ。creepy。

en: The natural light that is ambient in daytime, being mostly sunlight (both direct and indirect, on either sunny days or cloudy days).
A light source that simulates daylight.
To expose to daylight
To provide sources of natural illumination such as skylights or windows.

daylight.ety: From Middle English daye-lighte, dey liȝht, dailiȝt, day-liht, dai-liht (also as days lyȝt, daies liht), equivalent to day + light. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Deegeslucht, Daisljoacht (“daylight”), West Frisian deiljocht (“daylight”), Dutch daglicht (“daylight”), German Tageslicht (“daylight”).

ex.en: He had his car stolen in broad daylight.
ex.ja: 彼は真っ昼間に車を盗まれた。

ex.en: It scared the daylights out of him.
ex.ja: 彼はびっくりして肝を冷やした。

ex.en: Daylight Savings Time starts on April third.
ex.ja: サマータイムは、4月3日からです。

note.ja: day（日）+ light（光）。「日光・昼間」。

en: To uncover; physically expose to view.
To expose to the knowledge of others; to make known; state openly; reveal (something).

ex.en: You ought not to have disclosed the secret.
ex.ja: あなたはその秘密を漏らすべきではなかったのに。

ex.en: He should disclose everything and face the music.
ex.ja: 彼はすべてを明らかにして潔く責任を取るべきです。

ex.en: His secret will be disclosed soon.
ex.ja: 彼の秘密は近々ばれるだろう。

note.ja: dis（否定・開いて）+ clos（閉じる）+ e。閉じていたものを開く →「明らかにする・暴露する」。

en: A female deer; also used of similar animals such as antelope (less commonly a goat, as nanny is also used).
A female fallow deer.

doe.ety:

ex.en: I think your theory does not hold water.

ex.en: Faith which does not doubt is dead faith.

To push with the elbow or elbows; to forge ahead using the elbows to assist.

ex.en: I found at my elbow a pretty girl.
ex.ja: すぐ近くにかわいい子がいるのを知った。

ex.en: She hurt her elbow when she fell down.
ex.ja: 彼女は転んでひじを痛めた。

ex.en: Don't put your elbows on the table.
ex.ja: テーブルにひじをついてはいけません。

en: With zealous fervor; excited, motivated.
Relating to enthusiasm, or divine possession.

ex.ja: 今度の新しい仕事にジョージはとても熱中している。

ex.ja: 彼は人々が興奮しているときにはいつも離れている。

ex.en: This book is a result of his enthusiastic research.
ex.ja: この本は彼の熱心な研究の成果である。

en: Resentful desire of something possessed by another or others (but not limited to material possessions).
An object of envious notice or feeling.

To resentfully or discontentedly desire (something someone else has that one lacks).

ex.ja: 彼は友人たちの羨望の的であった。

ex.en: Their envy was directed toward her beauty.
ex.ja: 彼女らの妬みは彼女の美しさに向けられた。

note.ja: ラテン語 invidia（嫉妬）= in（〜に向かって）+ vid（見る）。（敵意を込めて）じっと見ること →「ねたみ・うらやむ」。

en: The state of being banished from one's home or country.
Someone who is banished from their home or country.
To send (someone or something) into exile.

exile.ety: From Middle English exil, borrowed from Old French essil, exil, from Latin exsilium, exilium (“state of exile”), derived from exsul, exul (“exiled person”).

ex.en: The criminal was sent into exile.
ex.ja: 犯人は国外に追放された。

ex.en: The exile yearned for his home.
ex.ja: その亡命者は故国への思いに胸を焦がした。

note.ja: ラテン語 exilium（追放）から。ex（外へ）+ salire（跳ぶ）とも言われる。「国の外へ出されること」→「亡命・追放」。

en: The act of utilizing something; industry.
The improper use of something for selfish purposes.

exploitation.ety: Borrowed from French exploitation, from exploiter (“exploit”), from Latin explicō (“unfold, deploy”). By surface analysis, exploit + -ation.

ex.en: Capitalism is the exploitation of man by man. Communism is the exact opposite.
ex.ja: 資本主義とは人間による人間の搾取である。共産主義はその真逆だ。

note.ja: exploit（利用する）+ -ation。ラテン語 explicitum（広げられた）から。ex（外へ）+ plicare（折る）。「たたんだものを広げて活用する」→「開発・搾取」。explicit と同じ。

en: A semi-solid to almost solid colloid of a solid and a liquid, such as jelly, cheese or opal.
A food preparation or dish in the form of a flavored gel.
To apply (cosmetic) gel to (the hair, etc).
To convert (a substance) into gel form.

en: The branch of biology that deals with the transmission and variation of inherited characteristics, in particular chromosomes and DNA.
The genetic makeup of a specific individual or species.

genetics.ety: From Ancient Greek γένεσις (génesis, “origin”). Coined by English biologist William Bateson in 1905 in a letter to zoologist Adam Sedgwick, and first used publicly by Bateson at a lecture to the International Conference on Plant Hybridization in 1906.

note.ja: gene（遺伝子）+ -tics（学）。ギリシャ語 genos（生まれ・種族）。genesis、generate と同じ gen。

A female goose.

ex.en: Why does that goose sit on her eggs?
ex.ja: なぜあのがちょうは卵の上に座っているのですか。

ex.en: Three women and a goose make a market.
ex.ja: 女３人と鵞鳥一羽で市ができる。

ex.en: He had a shot at the goose.
ex.ja: 彼はガンに向かって発砲した。

note.ja: 古英語 gōs から。複数形 geese。ドイツ語 Gans と同じ。gander（雄のガチョウ）。

en: A grating; a grid of wire or a sheet of material with a pattern of holes or slots, usually used to protect something while allowing the p…
The criss-cross pieces that separate panes of glass in a window.
To cook (food) on a grill; to barbecue.
To cook food under the element of a stove or only under the top element of an oven – (US) broil, (cooking) salamander.

grill.ety: 1655, from French gril, from Middle French gril, from Old French greïl, graïl (“gridiron”), from graïlle (“grate, grating”), from Latin crātīcula (“gridiron”), diminutive of crātis (“hurdle, wickerwork”), q.v. Related to griddle, hurdle.

ex.en: I don't like grilled fish, let alone raw fish.
ex.ja: 焼き魚は好きではありません、ましてや生魚は言うまでもありません。

ex.en: Tom took the meat off the grill.
ex.ja: トムはグリルから肉を取り出した。

ex.en: He ordered one grilled fish dinner.
ex.ja: 彼は焼き魚定食一人前を注文した。

note.ja: フランス語 gril（焼き網）から。ラテン語 craticula（小さな格子）。「焼き網で焼く」→ 火であぶるように「問い詰める」。

en: The rear part of the foot, where it joins the leg.
The part of a shoe's sole which supports the foot's heel.
To follow at somebody's heels; to chase closely.
To cause to follow at somebody’s heels (transitive).

heel.ety:
From Middle English hele, from Old English hēla, from Proto-West Germanic *hą̄hilō, from Proto-Germanic *hanhilaz, diminutive of Proto-Germanic *hanhaz (“heel, hock”), equivalent to hock + -le. More at hock.
Compare North Frisian haiel, West Frisian hyl, Dutch hiel, German Low German Hiel, Danish and Norwegian hæl, Swedish häl.

ex.en: He's head over heels in love with Mary.
ex.ja: 彼はメアリーにすっかり首ったけだ。

ex.en: He fell from the roof head over heels.
ex.ja: 彼は屋根からまっさかさまに落ちた。

ex.en: He fell head over heels into the pool.
ex.ja: 彼は真っ逆様にプールに落ちた。

note.ja: 古英語 hēla から。「かかと・ヒール」。

en: Of or relating to a hero or heroine; supremely noble.
Courageous; displaying heroism.
A heroic verse.

heroic.ety: Partly from Middle French heroïque and partly from Latin hērōicus. By surface analysis, hero + -ic.

ex.en: He is a very heroic figure.
ex.ja: 非常に英雄的な人物です。

ex.en: It was heroic of them to oppose the enemy.
ex.ja: 彼等が敵に向かうとはあっぱれであった。

note.ja: hero（英雄）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 hērōs（半神の英雄）。「英雄的な」。

en: A small, simple one-storey dwelling or shelter, often with just one room, and generally built of readily available local materials.
A small wooden shed.
Called by the quarterback to prepare the team for a play.

hut.ety:
From Middle English *hutte, hotte, from both Old English hōd and Old English hȳdan (“to hide”) and influenced by Anglo-Norman hute or hutte, from Middle French hutte, from Old French hute (“hut”), hute (“cottage”), from Old High German hutta (“hut, cottage”), from Proto-Germanic *hudjǭ, *hudjō (“hut”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewt- (“to deck; cover; covering; skin”).
Cognate with German Hütte (“hut”), Dutch hut (“hut”), West Frisian hutte (“hut”), Saterland Frisian Hutte (“hut”), Danish hytte (“hut”), Norwegian Bokmål hytte (“hut”), Swedish hydda (“hut”). Related to hide.

ex.en: There used to be a hut about here.
ex.ja: 以前はこのあたりに小屋があった。

ex.en: This hut is in danger of falling down.
ex.ja: この小屋は倒壊のおそれがある。

ex.en: We spent a night at the mountain hut.
ex.ja: 山小屋で一夜を明かした。

note.ja: フランス語 hutte から。ゲルマン系で「覆うもの」。hide（隠す）と同系。

en: A person confined to an institution such as a prison (as a convict) or hospital (as a patient).
A person who shares a residence (such as a hotel guest, a lodger, or a student living on campus), or other place.

ex.en: Tom was a model inmate.
ex.ja: トムは模範囚だった。

ex.en: Society is an insane asylum run by the inmates.
ex.ja: 社会は患者によって運営されている精神病院です。

ex.en: The inmate was doing time for a burglary conviction.
ex.ja: 囚人は強盗罪により服役していた。

note.ja: in（中に）+ mate（仲間）。「中にいる仲間」→「収容者」。

en: To teach by giving instructions.
To tell (someone) what they must or should do.

instruct.ety: From Latin īnstrūctus, perfect passive participle of īnstruō (“I instruct; I arrange, furnish, or provide”).

ex.en: He instructed me to go to bed early.
ex.ja: 彼は私に早く寝るように命じた。

ex.en: The doctor instructed me to go on a diet.
ex.ja: 医者は私にダイエットをするように指示した。

ex.en: He instructed students in history at school.
ex.ja: 彼は学校で歴史を教えていた。

note.ja: in（中に）+ struct（積む）。（知識を）中に積み上げる →「教える・指示する」。

en: A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering.
A small flat piece of material used to protect a surface from anything hot or rough; a coaster.
To cover, protect or decorate with mats.
To form a thick, tangled mess; to interweave into, or like, a mat; to entangle.

Cognate with German Matte (“mat”), Danish måtte (“mat”), Faroese and Icelandic motta (“rug, mat”), Norwegian matte (“mat, rug”), Swedish matta (“carpet, rug, mat”).

ex.en: He lay on the mat at full length.
ex.ja: 彼は畳の上に大の字になった。

ex.en: The dog was sleeping on the mat.
ex.ja: その犬はマットの上で寝ていた。

ex.en: The key is under the mat.
ex.ja: 鍵はマットの下です。

note.ja: ラテン語 matta（い草の敷物）から。「敷物・マット」。

en: A situation, by legal privilege or other agreement, in which solely one party (company, cartel etc.) exclusively provides a particular pr…
An exclusive control over the trade or production of a commodity or service through exclusive possession.

monopoly.ety: From Latin monopōlium, from Ancient Greek μονοπώλιον (monopṓlion, “a right of exclusive sale”), from μόνος (mónos, “sole”) + πωλέω (pōléō, “to barter, sell”). By surface analysis, mono- + -poly.

ex.en: Our store has a monopoly on this item.
ex.ja: これは当店の専売です。

ex.en: He was opposed to monopolies.
ex.ja: 彼は独占に反対していた。

ex.en: Postal services are a government monopoly.
ex.ja: 郵政事業は政府の独占事業です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 monos（1つの）+ pōlein（売る）。「1人だけが売ること」→「独占」。

en: An excessively violent or vicious attack; an atrocity.
An offensive, immoral or indecent act.
To cause or commit an outrage upon; to treat with violence or abuse.
To inspire feelings of outrage in.

outrage.ety:
From Middle English outrage, from Old French outrage, oultrage (“excess”), from Vulgar Latin *ultrāticum ("a going beyond"), derived from Latin ultrā (“beyond”). Later reanalysed as out- + rage, whence the contemporary pronunciation, though neither of these are etymologically related.
The verb is from Middle English outragen, from Old French oultragier.

ex.en: The outraged employee resigned at once.
ex.ja: かんかんに怒った社員は、即刻会社を辞めた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 outrage（度を越すこと）から。outre（超えて）、ultra と同じ。out + rage（激怒）と思われがちだが別。「度を越した行為」→「暴挙・激怒」。

en: Routine work involving written documents.
Written documents.

ex.en: I don't have time to do all the paperwork.
ex.ja: 全ての事務処理をやってる暇なんてないよ。

ex.en: I never have time to get through all the paperwork.
ex.ja: 全ての事務処理をやってる暇なんてないよ。

ex.en: We were bogged down in a morass of paperwork.
ex.ja: 私たちは書類事務の泥沼に陥っていた。

note.ja: paper（書類）+ work（仕事）。「書類仕事」。

Exactly at a specific time.

ex.en: Medical help arrives promptly after an accident.
ex.ja: 事故があるとすぐに救急医療隊が到着する。

ex.en: Any orders you place with us will be processed promptly.
ex.ja: 貴社からのどんなご注文にも、迅速に対処します。

An offensive action made immediately after a parried one.

en: A (usually rigid), flat, rectangular measuring or drawing device with graduations in units of measurement; a straightedge with markings.
A person who rules or governs; someone or something that exercises dominion or controlling power over others.
To beat with a ruler (as a traditional school punishment).

ruler.ety: From Middle English reuler; equivalent to rule + -er.

ex.en: I bought a book and he a ruler.
ex.ja: 私は本を買い、彼は定規を買った。

ex.en: Measure the length of the stick with a ruler.
ex.ja: ものさしでその棒の長さを測りなさい。

ex.en: A ruler helps one to draw a straight line.
ex.ja: 定規は直線を引くのに役立つ。

note.ja: rule（支配する・定規）+ -er。ラテン語 regula（まっすぐな棒・規則）。「まっすぐ測るもの」→「定規」、「規則で治める人」→「支配者」。regular と同じ。

en: Genuine, honest, and free from pretense or deceit; heartfelt.
Meant truly or earnestly.

sincere.ety: From Middle French sincere, from Latin sincerus (“genuine”), from Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“together”) (whence English sam) + *ḱer- (“grow”) (whence Latin Ceres, the goddess of harvest, etymon of cereal). Not from sine (“without”) + cera (“wax”), which is a folk etymology; see Wikipedia page.

ex.en: I do not doubt that he is sincere.
ex.ja: 私は彼が誠実であることを疑わない。

ex.en: He is sincere in what he says.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉には表裏がない。

ex.en: She is not quite sincere in what she says.
ex.ja: 彼女の言うことはそっくり本心からとは言えない。

note.ja: ラテン語 sincerus（純粋な・混じりけのない）から。「心からの・誠実な」。

en: The action of moving along a surface (ice or ground) using skates.
The sport of moving along a surface using skates.

ex.en: I would often go skating on the lake.
ex.ja: よく湖へスケートに行ったものだ。

ex.en: Have you ever tried skating on the river?
ex.ja: その川でスケートしたことがありますか。

ex.en: After the accident, Tom decided to stop skating.
ex.ja: 事故に遭った以来、トムはスケートをしないことを決めた。

note.ja: skate（スケートをする）+ -ing。skate はオランダ語 schaats（すべるもの）から。

en: The killing of animals, generally for food.
A massacre; the killing of a large number of people.
To butcher animals, generally for food.
To massacre people in large numbers.

slaughter.ety: From Middle English slaughter, from Old Norse *slahtr, later sláttr, from Proto-Germanic *slahtrą, from Proto-Germanic *slahaną. Equivalent to slay + -ter (as in laughter). Eventually derived from Proto-Indo-European *slak- (“to hit, strike, throw”). Related with Dutch slachten, German schlachten, Finnish lahdata (all “to slaughter”).

ex.en: The slaughter of the prisoners was a barbarous act.
ex.ja: 捕虜を虐殺したのは残忍な行為だ。

ex.en: The lambs were slaughtered for market.
ex.ja: 子羊たちは屠殺され市場に出された。

ex.en: Bulls make money, bears make money, hogs get slaughtered.
ex.ja: 強気な者はお金を儲け、弱気な者はお金を儲け、欲深い取引者は損失ぞ。

note.ja: 北欧語 slátr（屠殺した肉）から。slay（殺す）と同じ祖先。

en: The reproductive cell or gamete of the male; a spermatozoon.
Sperm oil; whale oil from a sperm whale; spermaceti.

sperm.ety: From Middle English sperme, from Latin sperma, from Ancient Greek σπέρμα (spérma, “seed, semen”). Compare also Old French esperme, sparme.

ex.en: I had an artificial insemination with sperm from my husband.
ex.ja: 配偶者間人工授精を受けました。

ex.en: The sperm whale can dive to a depth of 1,000 meters.
ex.ja: マッコウクジラは、1,000メートルの深さまで潜ることができる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 sperma（種）から。speirein（種をまく）。spore（胞子）も同じ。

en: To drop something so that it spreads out or makes a mess; to accidentally pour.
To spread out or fall out, as above.
Any thing that has been spilled; the resulting mess.
A fall or stumble.

spill.ety:
From Middle English spillen, from Old English spillan, spildan (“to kill, destroy, waste”), from Proto-West Germanic *spilþijan, from Proto-Germanic *spilþijaną (“to spoil, kill, murder”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pel- (“to sunder, split, rend, tear”).
Cognate with Dutch spillen (“to use needlessly, waste”), French gaspiller ("to waste, squander" < Germanic), Bavarian spillen (“to split, cleave, splinter”), Danish spilde (“to spill, waste”), Swedish spilla (“to spill, waste”), Icelandic spilla (“to contaminate, spoil”). See also spool.

ex.en: It is no use crying over spilt milk.
ex.ja: 過ぎ去ったことを嘆いてもしょうがない。

ex.en: There is no use crying over spilt milk.
ex.ja: 覆水盆に返らず。

ex.en: I completely spilled the coffee I just bought.
ex.ja: 買ったばかりのコーヒーを全部こぼしちゃった。

note.ja: 古英語 spillan（殺す・浪費する）から。「むだにする」→「こぼす」。

ex.en: Her studies are improving slowly but steadily.

en: An area of wet (water-saturated), spongy (soft) land, often with trees, generally a rich ecosystem for certain plants and animals but ill…
A place or situation that is foul or where progress is difficult.
To drench or fill with water.
To overwhelm; to make too busy, or overrun the capacity of.

swamp.ety: Early attestations (starting in 1624) are from North America, but the term was probably in local use in Britain earlier. The etymology is not entirely certain; it is probably a fusion of Middle English swam (“swamp, muddy pool, bog, marsh”, also “fungus, mushroom”) — from Old English swamm (“mushroom, fungus, sponge”), from Proto-West Germanic *swamm, from Proto-Germanic *swambaz, *swammaz — and Middle English sompe (“marsh, morass”), from either Middle Dutch somp, sump (“marsh, swamp”) or Middle Low German sump (“marsh, swamp”) (from Old Saxon *sump (“swamp, marsh”)), both from Proto-West Ger

ex.en: Twelve percent of Russia's territory is covered in swamps.
ex.ja: ロシアの領土の12%は、湿地に覆われています。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。sump（汚水だめ）と同系とされる。「沼地」→ 沼に沈めるように「圧倒する」。

One whose grace etc. suggests a swan.
To travel or move about in an aimless, idle, or pretentiously casual way.

Spelling modified by influence of Middle French cours (“course”). Doublet of discursus.

ex.en: In their discourse after dinner, they talked about politics.
ex.ja: 夕食後の談話で彼らは政治について話し合った。

note.ja: dis（あちこちへ）+ cours（走る）+ e。（話が）あちこち走ること →「講演・談話・言説」。

Being in a position of power, authority or ascendancy over others.

note.ja: dominant（支配的な）+ -ance。「優位・支配」。

From the perspective of economics or an economy.

en: A heroic or extraordinary deed.
An achievement.
To use (something) to someone's advantage, such as one's own benefit or a society's benefit.
To make unfair use of someone else's labor, person, or property to one's own advantage.

ex.en: The company exploited its workers through low wages.
ex.ja: 会社は従業員を低賃金で不当に利用した。

ex.en: He exploited his position to build up his fortune.
ex.ja: 財を成すため、彼は地位を利用した。

ex.en: Employers sometimes exploit their workers.
ex.ja: 雇い主は、時に従業員を搾取する。

note.ja: 「利用する」は上の exploitation と同じ。名詞「偉業」は「広げて成し遂げたこと」から。

en: An event or a display where fireworks are set off.
A boisterous or violent event or situation.

fireworks.ety: From fire + work(s). The similarity with Dutch vuurwerk and German Feuerwerk, both “fireworks”, is hardly coincidental. Since the word was apparently first attested in English circa 1575, probably from the Dutch (1540), from the German (sense early 16th c.), from Middle High German viurwerc (14th c. as “fuel, firewood”). A spread from the south northwards is also in line with the fact that the first European fireworks were produced in Italy in the late 14th century.

ex.en: The fireworks were set off on all sides.
ex.ja: 花火が四方八方であげられた。

ex.en: It's easy to see the fireworks from over there.
ex.ja: あそこなら花火が見やすいよ。

ex.en: As soon as it gets dark, the fireworks will start.
ex.ja: 暗くなったらすぐに花火がはじまるよ。

note.ja: fire（火）+ works（細工物）。「火の細工」→「花火」。

en: A person who is not a serf or slave.
A burgher with full freedom of a city, as opposed to nobles, outsiders, bondsmen, and others.

freeman.ety: From Old English frēomann, equivalent to free + -man and paralleled by similar constructions in other Germanic languages. Doublet of preman.

ex.en: Hello, is Mr Freeman in?
ex.ja: もしもし、フリーマン氏はおられますか。

note.ja: free（自由な）+ man。「自由民」→「名誉市民」。

en: A passage that can be closed by use of a gate.
A place regarded as giving access to somewhere.
To make available using a gateway, or access point.

ex.en: A car was blocking the gateway.
ex.ja: 車が通路を防いでいた。

note.ja: gate（門）+ way（道）。「門の通り道」→「入り口・玄関口」。

en: Dampness, especially that of the air.
The amount of water vapour in the air.

humidity.ety: From Middle English humidite, borrowed from Old French humidité, from Medieval Latin hūmiditās, from Latin ūmidus (“damp, moist, wet”). By surface analysis, humid + -ity.

ex.en: The humidity is 80%?! It must be really close!
ex.ja: 湿度が80パーセントだって？蒸し暑いはずだよ。

ex.en: This high humidity makes me feel tired.
ex.ja: この高湿度のせいで、私は疲れた感じがする。

ex.en: The humidity is very high, isn't it?
ex.ja: 湿度がすごく高いですね。

note.ja: humid（湿った）+ -ity。ラテン語 umere（湿っている）。humor（もと「体液」）と同系。

en: The work of one who makes images or visible representation of objects.
Imitation work.

imagery.ety: From Middle English ymagerie, from Middle French imagerie; equivalent to image + -ry.

note.ja: image（像）+ -ery。ラテン語 imago（像・写し）。「像の集まり」→「イメージ・比喩表現」。imitate と同系。

en: Naturally as part or consequence of something.

inherent.ety:

ex.ja: その問題はこのシステムに固有のものだ。

ex.en: That is a characteristic inherent in him.
ex.ja: それが彼本来の性格なのだ。

ex.en: The instinct for survival is inherent in every living thing.
ex.ja: 生存本能はあらゆる生物に固有のものである。

note.ja: in（中に）+ haerere（くっつく）+ -ent。「中にくっついている」→「本来備わっている」。adhere（くっつく）、coherent も同じ。

en: Within the land; relatively remote from the ocean or from open water; interior.
Limited to the land, or to inland routes; not passing on, or over, the sea.
The interior part of a country.
Into, or towards, the interior of the land, away from the coast.

inland.ety: From Middle English inland, inlond, from Old English inland, equivalent to in- + land. Compare West Frisian ynlân (“inland”), German Inland (“inland”), Danish indland (“inland”), Swedish inland (“inland”), Norwegian innland (“inland”). Compare also Dutch binnenland.

ex.en: I was born in the inland, in an unremarkable town.
ex.ja: 私は、内陸部のなんということもない町に生まれた。

ex.en: He traveled through inland China.
ex.ja: 彼は中国の内陸を旅行しました。

ex.en: And me, I was born in a nondescript town in the inland.
ex.ja: 私は、内陸部のなんということもない町に生まれた。

note.ja: in（内に）+ land（陸）。「陸の内側の」→「内陸の」。

en: Absence of responsibility for a crime, tort, etc.
Lack of understanding about sensitive subjects such as sexuality and crime.

innocence.ety: Inherited from Middle English innocence, from Old French innocence, inocence, from Latin innocentia. Doublet of innocency. Displaced native Old English unsċyld.

ex.en: You must not take advantage of her innocence.
ex.ja: 君は彼女の無邪気さに付け込んではいけない。

ex.en: I have a firm belief in his innocence.
ex.ja: 僕は彼の無実を堅く信じている。

ex.en: In due time, his innocence will be proved.
ex.ja: 時が来れば彼の無罪が証明されるだろう。

note.ja: in（否定）+ nocere（害する）+ -ence。「害のないこと」→「無罪・無邪気」。innocent、nuisance と同じ。

en: An island, usually very small. Compare with islet.

isle.ety: From Middle English ile, yle (with s added, similar to English island), borrowed from Old French ille, idle, isle, from Latin insula. Not related to island. Doublet of insula.

note.ja: ラテン語 insula（島）から古フランス語を経た語。island とは別語源だが、island の s はこの語の影響。

en: Any of several woody, climbing, or trailing evergreen plants of the genus Hedera.
Any similar plant of any genus.

ivy.ety: From Middle English ivi, from Old English īfiġ, from Proto-West Germanic *ibig, *ibag, *ibah, from Proto-Germanic *ibahs (compare West Flemish iefte, Low German Eiloov, Ieloof, German Efeu), from Proto-Indo-European *(h₁)ebʰ- (compare Welsh efwr (“black elder”), Ancient Greek ἴφυον (íphuon, “spike-lavender, Lavandula Spica”)).

ex.en: The side of the house was covered with ivy.
ex.ja: 家の横はつたで覆われていた。

ex.en: The walls are hidden by ivy.
ex.ja: 壁はツタで覆われている。

ex.en: The wall is partly covered with ivy.
ex.ja: その壁は部分的につたで覆われている。

note.ja: 古英語 īfig から。「ツタ」。Ivy League は校舎がツタに覆われた名門大学から。

en: A reason, explanation, or excuse which someone believes provides convincing, morally acceptable support for behavior or for a belief or o…
The forgiveness of sin.

justification.ety: From Middle English justificacioun, justification, from Middle French justification, from Late Latin iustificationem, justificationem < iustificatio, from iustifico, from Latin iustus.

ex.en: You have no justification to say something like that.
ex.ja: お前にそんなこと言われる筋合いねえよ。

note.ja: justify（正当化する）+ -ication。ラテン語 justus（正しい）+ facere（する）。「正しいとすること」。just、justice と同じ jus。

en: A hierarchically structured secret organisation engaged in illegal activities like distribution of narcotics, gambling and extortion.
A crime syndicate.

mafia.ety: See Mafia. The sense "entity which attempts to control a specified arena" makes an analogy to crime-syndicate mafias' attempts to control certain kinds of business in the regions in which they exist.

ex.ja: 麻薬のためのお金やマフィアの資金は殺人の報酬であることが多い。

ex.en: The Mafia uses legitimate business operations as a front.
ex.ja: マフィアは隠れみのに合法的な事業を展開している。

ex.en: Tom made the decision to cut ties with the mafia and start life over.
ex.ja: トムはマフィアと縁を切って人生をやり直す決意をした。

note.ja: イタリア語（シチリア方言）mafia（大胆さ・虚勢）から。

en: Jolly and full of high spirits; happy.
Festive and full of fun and laughter.
An English wild cherry.

merry.ety: From Middle English myrie, merie, mery, from Old English myrġe, myriġe (“pleasing, agreeable; pleasant, sweet, delightful; melodious”), from Proto-West Germanic *murgī (“short, slow, leisurely”), from Proto-Germanic *murguz (“short, slow”), from Proto-Indo-European *mréǵʰus (“short”). Doublet of brief.

ex.en: The girls are making merry in the yard.
ex.ja: 彼女たちが庭ではしゃいでいる。

ex.en: The children are riding the merry-go-round.
ex.ja: 子どもたちは、メリーゴーランドに乗ってるよ。

ex.en: Little did I dream of hearing such a merry song.
ex.ja: そんなに楽しい歌を聞こうとは、夢にも思いませんでした。

note.ja: 古英語 myrge（楽しい）から。mirth（陽気さ）と同じ。Merry Christmas。

A person who travels attempting to spread a religion or creed (Particularly used in context of Christianity).
Relating to a (religious) mission.

en: A more extreme form of patriotism; the idea of a more extreme support for one's country, people or culture.
Support for the creation of a sovereign nation (which does not currently exist).

nationalism.ety: Borrowed from French nationalisme, equivalent to national + -ism.

ex.en: Their nationalism was one cause of the war.
ex.ja: 彼らの民族主義がその戦争の原因の一つだった。

ex.en: Nationalism is not to be confused with patriotism.
ex.ja: 国家主義と愛国心とを混同してはならない。

ex.en: You can't equate nationalism with fascism.
ex.ja: ナショナリズムをファシズムと同一視してはいけない。

note.ja: national（国の）+ -ism。nation はラテン語 natio（生まれ・民族）、nasci（生まれる）。

en: Mischievous; tending to misbehave or act badly (especially of a child).
Sexually provocative; now in weakened sense, risqué, cheeky.

naughty.ety: From late Middle English noughti, naughty (“evil, immoral, wicked”), from nought (“evil, immoral”) + -ī̆ (suffix forming adjectives). Analysable as naught + -y.

ex.en: The naughty boy got lost and looked around.
ex.ja: わんぱくな子は道に迷ってあたりを見回した。

ex.en: I can do nothing with this naughty boy.
ex.ja: 私はこのわんぱくな少年は手に負えない。

ex.en: Parents love their children however naughty they are.
ex.ja: 親というものは、どんなに腕白でも、子供を可愛がるものです。

note.ja: naught（無・ゼロ）+ -y。「何も持たない・取るに足りない」→「悪い」→「いたずらな」と意味が軽くなった。

en: To give (someone) notice (of some event).

notify.ety: From Middle English notifien, a borrowing from Old French notifier, notefiier.

ex.en: He notified the police of the traffic accident.
ex.ja: 彼は警察に交通事故を知らせた。

ex.en: You should notify the police at once.
ex.ja: すぐ警察に通報してください。

ex.en: He notified me that he would start at three.
ex.ja: 彼は３時に出発すると私に通知してきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 notus（知られた）+ facere（する）。「知られるようにする」→「知らせる」。notice、notification と同じ。

en: Of a person or entity: generally or widely known for something negative; infamous.
Of an act, situation, etc.: blameworthy in an obvious and offensive way; blatant, flagrant.

notorious.ety:

Nōtus is the perfect passive participle of nōscō (“to become acquainted with or learn about (something); (rare) to be familiar with, recognize”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (“to know; to recognize”).

ex.en: The notorious criminal was caught yesterday.
ex.ja: その悪名高い犯罪者は昨日逮捕された。

ex.en: The city is notorious for its polluted air.
ex.ja: その都市は大気汚染がひどいことで有名だ。

ex.en: The store is notorious for charging high prices.
ex.ja: その店は値段が高いので有名だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 notorius（よく知られた）から。notus（知られた）。「よく知られた」→ 悪い意味で →「悪名高い」。

en: To do as ordered by (a person, institution etc), to act according to the bidding of.
To do as one is told.

obey.ety: From Middle English obeyen, from Anglo-Norman obeir, obeier et al., Old French obeir, from Latin oboediō (also obēdiō (“to listen to, harken, usually in extended sense, obey, be subject to, serve”)), from ob- (“before, near”) + audiō (“to hear”). In Latin, ob + audire would have been expected to become Classical Latin *obūdiō (compare in + claudō becoming inclūdō), but it has been theorized that the usual law court associations of the word for obeying encouraged a false archaism from ū to oe, to oboediō (compare Old Latin oinos → Classical Latin ūnus).

ex.en: It is necessary that everybody obey the law.
ex.ja: だれでも法律をまもることは必要だ。

ex.en: You don't have to obey such a law.
ex.ja: そんな法に従わなくてもよい。

ex.en: I must request you to obey my orders.
ex.ja: 私の命令には従ってもらうようお願いいたします。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ audire（聞く）。「言うことに耳を傾ける」→「従う」。audio、audience と同じ aud。

Relating to the action of organizing something.

Unqualified and unreserved.
Total or complete.
To release a player outright, without conditions.

outright.ety: From Middle English outright. By surface analysis, out + right.

ex.ja: 私はこれを即金で買った。

ex.en: I had expected an outright refusal, but to my surprise she agreed.
ex.ja: あっさり断られると思いきや、彼女は承諾してくれました。

note.ja: out（完全に）+ right（まっすぐ）。「完全に・きっぱりと」。

en: To an excessive degree.
To a high degree; very.

ex.ja: あの人って、自意識過剰だよね。

ex.ja: 寛大すぎることが彼の最大の欠点です。

en: An omission; something that is left out, missed, or forgotten.
Supervision or management.

oversight.ety: From over- + sight. Verb sense 2 is a semantic loan from German Aufsicht.

ex.en: There is big oversight in that plan.
ex.ja: その計画には大きな見落としがある。

ex.en: It was simply an oversight.
ex.ja: それは単なる手落ちだ。

ex.en: I suspect that there was an oversight in the examination.
ex.ja: 検査に手落ちがあったのではないだろうか。

en: Any of various big cats with black fur; most especially, the black-coated leopard of Africa and Asia.
Any big cat of the genus Panthera.

panther.ety: From Middle English pantere, panter, from Old French pantere, from Latin panthēra, from Ancient Greek πάνθηρ (pánthēr, “panther”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 panthēr から。「ヒョウ・ピューマ」。

Of or pertaining to the Persian people.
A native or inhabitant of the historical polity of Persia (for example, any of the various Persian empires).
A member of the ethnic group indigenous to Persis and the Iranian plateau that forms the majority of the population of modern-day Iran.

ex.ja: ペルシャ猫がテーブルの下で眠っていた。

ex.en: There is an old story about a Persian cat.
ex.ja: ペルシャ猫に関連した古いお話しがあります。

ex.en: I think I want to study Persian.
ex.ja: ペルシャ語を勉強したいと思っています。

note.ja: Persia + -an。古代ペルシャの地方名 Pārsa から。

An early sample or model built to test a concept or process.
To create a prototype of.

ex.en: Some people love pumpkin pie and others hate it.
ex.ja: パンプキンパイが大好きっていう人もいれば、大嫌いっていう人もいるわ。

en: An inclined surface that connects two levels; an incline.
An interchange, a road that connects a freeway to a surface street or another freeway.
To behave violently; to rage.
To (cause to) change value, often at a steady rate.

en: Subtle, scrupulous, carefully thought out.
Developed, improved.

ex.ja: 彼女は非常に上品な女性です。

ex.en: His speech is very refined.
ex.ja: 彼の話し方はたいへん洗練されている。

ex.en: She's a very refined lady.
ex.ja: 彼女は本当に洗練された女性だよ。

ex.ja: 朝食前の散歩は気分がよい。

ex.ja: 暑い天候のとき、コップ１杯の冷たい水はとても爽やかだ。

note.ja: refresh（元気づける）+ -ing。re（再び）+ fresh（新鮮な）。「さわやかな・新鮮な」。

en: The act of refusing.
Depth or point at which well or borehole drilling cannot continue.

refusal.ety: Inherited from Middle English refusell. By surface analysis, refuse + -al.

ex.ja: 彼女は私の申し出を素っ気なく断った。

ex.en: His reply was in effect a refusal.
ex.ja: 彼の返事は事実上は拒絶だった。

ex.en: He gave a flat refusal to his mother's request.
ex.ja: 彼はお母さんの頼みをにべもなくことわった。

en: Something that corrects or counteracts.
The legal means to recover a right or to prevent or obtain redress for a wrong.
To provide or serve as a remedy for.

remedy.ety: From Middle English remedie, from Old French *remedie, remede, from Latin remedium (“a remedy, cure”), from re- (“again”) + mederi (“to heal”). Doublet of remeid.

ex.en: This is an effective remedy for crime.
ex.ja: これは有効な犯罪防止対策だ。

ex.en: Your only remedy is to go to the law.
ex.ja: 唯一の解決法は法に訴えることだ。

ex.en: We have yet to discover an effective remedy for cancer.
ex.ja: 癌の効果的な治療法はまだ発見されていない。

note.ja: re（再び・すっかり）+ med（癒す）+ y。すっかり癒すもの →「治療法・救済策」。medicine と同じ med。

en: To set back to the initial state.
To set to zero.
The act of resetting to the initial state.
The act of setting to zero.

en: Wise.

ex.ja: 彼は賢者だ。

To cut anything in this fashion.
An instance of shaving.
A thin slice; a shaving.

Nausea; qualmishness; as, sickness of stomach.

sickness.ety: Inherited from Middle English sikness, from Old English sēocnes, sēocness, sēocnys, sēocnyss. By surface analysis, sick + -ness.

ex.en: Assassination has never changed the history of the world.
ex.ja: 暗殺が世界の歴史を変えたことはない。

ex.en: Older people still remember the Kennedy assassination.
ex.ja: 年配の人はまだケネディー暗殺事件を覚えている。

ex.en: Investigators uncovered an assassination plot.
ex.ja: 捜査員らは暗殺計画を摘発しました。

note.ja: assassinate（暗殺する）+ -ion。アラビア語 ḥashshāshīn（大麻を使う者）。中世の暗殺教団の呼び名から。

en: To admit to the truth, particularly in the context of sins or crimes committed.
To acknowledge faith in; to profess belief in.

confess.ety:
From Middle English confessen, from Anglo-Norman confesser, from Old French confesser, from Latin confessus (Old French confés), past participle of cōnfiteor (“to confess, admit”) from con- + fateor (“to admit”). Displaced Middle English andetten (“to confess, admit”) (from Old English andettan). Doublet of confiteor.
Sense 6 is a semantic loan from Japanese 告(こく)白(はく) (kokuhaku).

ex.en: The man finally confessed what he had done.
ex.ja: その男はついに自分のしたことを白状した。

ex.en: "I care very deeply for you", she confessed.
ex.ja: 「すごくあなたが気になるの」と彼女は告白した。

ex.en: He confessed that he had committed the crime.
ex.ja: 彼は自分が罪を犯したと白状した。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ fateri（認める）。「すっかり認める」→「告白する・自白する」。confession。
